title: The Band: Instrument Station
strapline: Shake it, tap it, bang it — making music together and finding the beat.
intent: Children explore how instruments make sound and how they can change it — louder, softer, faster, slower.
Children find and keep a steady beat, the rhythmic foundation of music and, later, of reading.
Children play together, listening to each other, taking turns and making music as a group.
Children express feelings and ideas through sound, using music as a language of its own.
Children build vocabulary for sound and music — loud, quiet, tap, shake, ring, beat, fast, slow.
implementation: Offer a range of real instruments — shakers, drums, bells, claves, a tambourine, a xylophone — well cared for and available.
Let children explore freely first: how does this one sound, what happens if I hit it harder or softer?
Model finding the beat by playing along to a familiar song, tapping steadily on your knees or a drum.
Play copying games: 'can you play what I play?' — a short pattern for children to echo back.
Introduce loud and quiet, fast and slow through conducting — hands up high for loud, low for quiet.
Form a 'band' to accompany singing time, giving each child an instrument and a turn to lead.
Talk about the sounds and feelings — 'that drum sounds like thunder', 'the bells sound happy'.
key_questions: How does this instrument make its sound?
Can you make it louder? Quieter?
Can you copy the beat I'm playing?
Which instrument sounds happy — or scary?
Can we all play together and stop together?

impact.text: Children explore and change the sounds instruments make.
Children find and keep a steady beat.
Children copy and create simple rhythmic patterns.
Children play together, listening and taking turns.
Children use sound to express feelings and ideas.
Children use vocabulary for sound — loud, quiet, fast, slow, beat.

enhancements: A 'sound wall' outdoors — pots, pans and metal tubes to strike.
Home-made instruments the children build themselves (see the shakers card).
Recordings of different music styles to play along with.
Picture cards of loud/quiet and fast/slow to 'conduct' the band.
A microphone and simple recorder to hear the band played back.
Scarves and ribbons so some children dance while others play.

playing_exploring: Children explore every instrument to discover its sounds.
They experiment with how hard, fast and soft they can play.
active_learning: Children keep going to match the beat and copy a pattern.
Playing in a band gives them a shared goal to sustain.
creating_thinking: Children invent rhythms and choose sounds to express an idea.
They decide how to make music together and start and stop as one.
